sourcesContent:
export const scenarios = [
  {
    id: 'sim-01',
    title: 'Acute Appendicitis Evaluation',
    specialty: 'Emergency Medicine',
    difficulty: 'Intermediate',
    estimatedTime: '18 min',
    questionCount: 5,
    caseStages: [
      { id: 'presentation', title: 'Presentation', description: 'Review presenting symptoms and vital signs.' },
      { id: 'history', title: 'History', description: 'Gather key history and risk factors.' },
      { id: 'examination', title: 'Examination', description: 'Interpret physical exam findings.' },
      { id: 'diagnosis', title: 'Diagnosis', description: 'Formulate the leading diagnosis.' },
      { id: 'investigation', title: 'Investigation', description: 'Select appropriate tests and next steps.' }
    ],
    highlights: [
      'Use systematic history taking',
      'Pay attention to vital sign trends',
      'Match exam findings with likely diagnoses'
    ],
    recommendedAfter: 'Review case feedback and clinical reasoning resources.',
    description: 'Assess an adult patient presenting with abdominal pain and determine the next best diagnostic step.',
    learningObjectives: [
      'Recognize key signs of appendicitis',
      'Interpret abdominal exam findings',
      'Choose appropriate imaging studies'
    ],
    patient: {
      name: 'John Mwinyi',
      age: '45 years',
      sex: 'Male',
      chiefComplaint: 'Fever and abdominal pain',
      vitalSigns: {
        temperature: '38.7°C',
        heartRate: '104 bpm',
        bloodPressure: '130/85 mmHg',
        respiratoryRate: '20/min'
      },
      history: 'The patient reports 24 hours of worsening right lower quadrant pain, nausea, and low-grade fever. He has decreased appetite and no bowel movements today.'
    },
    questions: [
      {
        id: 'q1',
        question: 'What is the most likely diagnosis?',
        options: [
          'Acute appendicitis',
          'Acute cholecystitis',
          'Gastroenteritis',
          'Peptic ulcer disease'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Acute appendicitis',
        explanation: 'Right lower quadrant pain with fever and anorexia is classic for acute appendicitis.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q2',
        question: 'Which physical exam finding best supports the diagnosis?',
        options: [
          'Murphy sign',
          'McBurney point tenderness',
          'Psoas sign',
          'Cullen sign'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'McBurney point tenderness',
        explanation: 'McBurney point tenderness is a key exam finding in appendicitis.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q3',
        question: 'What is the next best diagnostic test?',
        options: [
          'Abdominal ultrasound',
          'Contrast CT scan',
          'Plain abdominal X-ray',
          'HIDA scan'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Contrast CT scan',
        explanation: 'CT scan is preferred for confirming appendicitis in adults.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q4',
        question: 'Which laboratory result is most expected?',
        options: [
          'Elevated lipase',
          'Leukocytosis',
          'Hypokalemia',
          'Elevated bilirubin'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Leukocytosis',
        explanation: 'Leukocytosis is common in acute appendicitis.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q5',
        question: 'What is the initial clinical management step?',
        options: [
          'Immediate laparotomy',
          'IV fluids and antibiotics',
          'Reassurance and discharge',
          'Endoscopy'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'IV fluids and antibiotics',
        explanation: 'Begin resuscitation and antibiotics before surgical intervention.'
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    id: 'sim-02',
    title: 'Pediatric Asthma Exacerbation',
    specialty: 'Pediatrics',
    difficulty: 'Beginner',
    estimatedTime: '15 min',
    questionCount: 4,
    caseStages: [
      { id: 'presentation', title: 'Presentation', description: 'Review presenting symptoms and vital signs.' },
      { id: 'history', title: 'History', description: 'Gather key history and risk factors.' },
      { id: 'examination', title: 'Examination', description: 'Interpret physical exam findings.' },
      { id: 'diagnosis', title: 'Diagnosis', description: 'Formulate the leading diagnosis.' },
      { id: 'investigation', title: 'Investigation', description: 'Select appropriate tests and next steps.' }
    ],
    highlights: [
      'Identify urgency in pediatric respiratory distress',
      'Differentiate mild and severe exacerbations',
      'Prioritize first-line therapy'
    ],
    recommendedAfter: 'Review pediatric airway management and asthma protocols.',
    description: 'Manage a child with acute wheezing and shortness of breath in the emergency department.',
    learningObjectives: [
      'Identify severity of asthma exacerbation',
      'Select initial therapy for pediatric asthma',
      'Monitor response to treatment'
    ],
    patient: {
      name: 'Amina Hassan',
      age: '9 years',
      sex: 'Female',
      chiefComplaint: 'Wheezing and shortness of breath',
      vitalSigns: {
        temperature: '37.8°C',
        heartRate: '118 bpm',
        bloodPressure: '110/72 mmHg',
        respiratoryRate: '30/min'
      },
      history: 'The patient has a history of asthma and presents with increased coughing, wheezing, and nocturnal symptoms after exposure to cold air.'
    },
    questions: [
      {
        id: 'q1',
        question: 'What is the first step in management?',
        options: [
          'Nebulized albuterol',
          'Oral corticosteroids',
          'Chest physiotherapy',
          'Intubation'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Nebulized albuterol',
        explanation: 'Bronchodilator therapy is first-line in acute asthma exacerbation.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q2',
        question: 'Which sign indicates a severe exacerbation?',
        options: [
          'Normal speech',
          'Tachypnea',
          'Accessory muscle use',
          'Mild wheezing'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Accessory muscle use',
        explanation: 'Accessory muscle use suggests increased work of breathing and severity.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q3',
        question: 'What additional treatment should be given?',
        options: [
          'IV antibiotics',
          'Oral antihistamine',
          'Systemic corticosteroids',
          'Sublingual immunotherapy'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Systemic corticosteroids',
        explanation: 'Corticosteroids reduce inflammation during moderate to severe exacerbations.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q4',
        question: 'When should the child be considered for hospitalization?',
        options: [
          'No prior history of asthma',
          'Mild symptoms at rest',
          'Poor response to bronchodilators',
          'Improved peak flow'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Poor response to bronchodilators',
        explanation: 'Failure to respond to initial therapy warrants admission.'
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    id: 'sim-03',
    title: 'Postoperative Wound Assessment',
    specialty: 'Surgery',
    difficulty: 'Advanced',
    estimatedTime: '22 min',
    questionCount: 5,
    caseStages: [
      { id: 'presentation', title: 'Presentation', description: 'Review presenting symptoms and vital signs.' },
      { id: 'history', title: 'History', description: 'Gather key history and risk factors.' },
      { id: 'examination', title: 'Examination', description: 'Interpret physical exam findings.' },
      { id: 'diagnosis', title: 'Diagnosis', description: 'Formulate the leading diagnosis.' },
      { id: 'investigation', title: 'Investigation', description: 'Select appropriate tests and next steps.' }
    ],
    highlights: [
      'Recognize postoperative infection signs',
      'Use vitals to guide escalation',
      'Choose imaging wisely'
    ],
    recommendedAfter: 'Review postoperative complication pathways and surgical consultation criteria.',
    description: 'Evaluate a postoperative patient with abdominal pain and assess for surgical complications.',
    learningObjectives: [
      'Recognize signs of wound infection',
      'Interpret postoperative vital signs',
      'Choose appropriate imaging for complications'
    ],
    patient: {
      name: 'Peter Omari',
      age: '62 years',
      sex: 'Male',
      chiefComplaint: 'Abdominal pain after surgery',
      vitalSigns: {
        temperature: '38.2°C',
        heartRate: '98 bpm',
        bloodPressure: '140/90 mmHg',
        respiratoryRate: '18/min'
      },
      history: 'The patient had a laparoscopic cholecystectomy three days ago and now reports increasing abdominal discomfort, nausea, and redness around the incision site.'
    },
    questions: [
      {
        id: 'q1',
        question: 'Which finding is most concerning for infection?',
        options: [
          'Mild nausea',
          'Incision erythema with purulent drainage',
          'Low-grade fever',
          'Fatigue'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Incision erythema with purulent drainage',
        explanation: 'Purulent drainage is a strong sign of wound infection.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q2',
        question: 'What imaging study is most appropriate?',
        options: [
          'Chest X-ray',
          'Abdominal CT scan',
          'Pelvic ultrasound',
          'Plain abdominal film'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Abdominal CT scan',
        explanation: 'CT is useful to evaluate postoperative abdominal complications.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q3',
        question: 'Which management step should be taken next?',
        options: [
          'Oral antibiotics only',
          'Open surgical exploration immediately',
          'IV antibiotics and close monitoring',
          'Discharge home'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'IV antibiotics and close monitoring',
        explanation: 'Start IV antibiotics and monitor before deciding on surgical intervention.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q4',
        question: 'What is the most likely diagnosis?',
        options: [
          'Atelectasis',
          'Wound infection',
          'Pulmonary embolism',
          'Ileus'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Wound infection',
        explanation: 'Incision changes and fever point to wound infection.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q5',
        question: 'Which specialty should be consulted?',
        options: [
          'Cardiology',
          'Infectious disease',
          'Surgery',
          'Endocrinology'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Surgery',
        explanation: 'Surgery should be involved for postoperative wound concerns.'
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    id: 'sim-04',
    title: 'Gestational Hypertension Management',
    specialty: 'Obstetrics & Gynecology',
    difficulty: 'Intermediate',
    estimatedTime: '20 min',
    questionCount: 4,
    caseStages: [
      { id: 'presentation', title: 'Presentation', description: 'Review presenting symptoms and vital signs.' },
      { id: 'history', title: 'History', description: 'Gather key history and risk factors.' },
      { id: 'examination', title: 'Examination', description: 'Interpret physical exam findings.' },
      { id: 'diagnosis', title: 'Diagnosis', description: 'Formulate the leading diagnosis.' },
      { id: 'investigation', title: 'Investigation', description: 'Select appropriate tests and next steps.' }
    ],
    highlights: [
      'Understand safe medication choices in pregnancy',
      'Track evolving blood pressure patterns',
      'Apply maternal-fetal assessment principles'
    ],
    recommendedAfter: 'Review hypertension management in pregnancy and antenatal monitoring.',
    description: 'Evaluate a pregnant patient with elevated blood pressure and determine safe management options.',
    learningObjectives: [
      'Identify gestational hypertension',
      'Interpret blood pressure thresholds in pregnancy',
      'Recommend appropriate antihypertensive therapy'
    ],
    patient: {
      name: 'Fatima Njoroge',
      age: '29 years',
      sex: 'Female',
      chiefComplaint: 'Headache and swelling',
      vitalSigns: {
        temperature: '36.8°C',
        heartRate: '88 bpm',
        bloodPressure: '150/95 mmHg',
        respiratoryRate: '18/min'
      },
      history: 'At 34 weeks gestation, the patient reports headaches and swelling in her hands. She has no history of hypertension before pregnancy.'
    },
    questions: [
      {
        id: 'q1',
        question: 'What is the most likely diagnosis?',
        options: [
          'Pre-eclampsia',
          'Gestational hypertension',
          'Chronic hypertension',
          'Hypotension'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Gestational hypertension',
        explanation: 'New hypertension after 20 weeks without proteinuria suggests gestational hypertension.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q2',
        question: 'Which medication is recommended during pregnancy?',
        options: [
          'Lisinopril',
          'Methyldopa',
          'Atenolol',
          'Losartan'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Methyldopa',
        explanation: 'Methyldopa is an antihypertensive safe in pregnancy.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q3',
        question: 'What additional test should be ordered?',
        options: [
          'Urinalysis for protein',
          'Liver biopsy',
          'Fetal MRI',
          'Echocardiogram'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Urinalysis for protein',
        explanation: 'Proteinuria assessment helps distinguish pre-eclampsia from gestational hypertension.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q4',
        question: 'What is the next best step after diagnosis?',
        options: [
          'Immediate delivery',
          'Observation only',
          'Close monitoring and medication',
          'Discharge without follow-up'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Close monitoring and medication',
        explanation: 'Monitor the patient and treat blood pressure appropriately in gestational hypertension.'
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    id: 'sim-05',
    title: 'Cardiac Chest Pain Assessment',
    specialty: 'Internal Medicine',
    difficulty: 'Advanced',
    estimatedTime: '24 min',
    questionCount: 5,
    caseStages: [
      { id: 'presentation', title: 'Presentation', description: 'Review presenting symptoms and vital signs.' },
      { id: 'history', title: 'History', description: 'Gather key history and risk factors.' },
      { id: 'examination', title: 'Examination', description: 'Interpret physical exam findings.' },
      { id: 'diagnosis', title: 'Diagnosis', description: 'Formulate the leading diagnosis.' },
      { id: 'investigation', title: 'Investigation', description: 'Select appropriate tests and next steps.' }
    ],
    highlights: [
      'Differentiate high-risk chest pain features',
      'Focus on rapid cardiac assessment',
      'Choose early diagnostic testing'
    ],
    recommendedAfter: 'Review acute coronary syndrome pathways and chest pain triage.',
    description: 'Assess a patient with chest pain and determine the most likely cardiac diagnosis.',
    learningObjectives: [
      'Interpret ECG changes',
      'Differentiate chest pain etiologies',
      'Select initial cardiac management steps'
    ],
    patient: {
      name: 'Lilian Achieng',
      age: '58 years',
      sex: 'Female',
      chiefComplaint: 'Chest pain and shortness of breath',
      vitalSigns: {
        temperature: '37.2°C',
        heartRate: '96 bpm',
        bloodPressure: '145/92 mmHg',
        respiratoryRate: '22/min'
      },
      history: 'The patient reports substernal chest pressure radiating to the left arm, associated with nausea and diaphoresis over the past hour.'
    },
    questions: [
      {
        id: 'q1',
        question: 'Which diagnosis is most likely?',
        options: [
          'Stable angina',
          'Acute myocardial infarction',
          'Pneumonia',
          'GERD'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Acute myocardial infarction',
        explanation: 'Typical chest pain with radiation and diaphoresis suggests MI.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q2',
        question: 'What initial test should be ordered?',
        options: [
          'Echocardiogram',
          'Troponin and ECG',
          'Chest CT',
          'Stress test'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Troponin and ECG',
        explanation: 'ECG and cardiac biomarkers are first-line for chest pain.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q3',
        question: 'Which medication is appropriate immediately?',
        options: [
          'IV antibiotics',
          'Sublingual nitroglycerin',
          'Oral ibuprofen',
          'Oral prednisone'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Sublingual nitroglycerin',
        explanation: 'Nitroglycerin can relieve ischemic chest pain acutely.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q4',
        question: 'What risk factor is most relevant in this patient?',
        options: [
          'Young age',
          'Female sex',
          'Hypertension',
          'Asthma'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Hypertension',
        explanation: 'Hypertension is a major risk factor for coronary artery disease.'
      },
      {
        id: 'q5',
        question: 'Which disposition is most appropriate?',
        options: [
          'Discharge home',
          'Admit for observation and cardiac workup',
          'Refer to endocrinology',
          'Schedule outpatient stress test'
        ],
        correctAnswer: 'Admit for observation and cardiac workup',
        explanation: 'Suspected MI requires admission and further evaluation.'
      }
    ]
  }
];
